name: Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh QL-7 Urban Air Quality Sensor Lattice
product_name: Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh QL-7 Urban Air Quality Sensor Lattice
description:
The AtmoMesh QL-7 is a distributed urban atmospheric monitoring network composed of approximately 340,000 individual sensor nodes deployed across GLMZ's built environment — embedded in streetlight housings, transit shelters, building facades, utility poles, and autonomous delivery drone docking stations. Each node continuously samples for 47 atmospheric compounds including industrial particulates, heavy metal aerosols, volatile organic compounds, radiological markers, and biological agents, transmitting compressed data packets every 90 seconds to Saltmarsh Telecom's regional atmospheric data hub. The network generates a real-time three-dimensional chemical map of the city's air column updated at city-block resolution, marketed to municipal authorities, industrial operators, and corporate health and safety administrators as the definitive environmental intelligence product for GLMZ.

The QL-7's sensor nodes use a hybrid electrochemical-optical detection architecture that achieves laboratory-grade sensitivity for priority compounds while drawing under 0.4 watts per node, allowing solar and kinetic parasitic power to sustain most nodes without grid connection. Saltmarsh's proprietary Atmospheric Intelligence Suite processes raw sensor feeds through Cinderblock AI pattern recognition to distinguish industrial emission events from background variation, flag novel compound signatures, and generate predictive dispersion models for incoming weather systems. The data product is sold on tiered subscription: industrial operators receive private plume attribution feeds, corporate clients receive district-level hazard forecasts, and public terminals display a simplified color-coded safety index that maps to GLMZ's official air quality tiers.

The gap between what the AtmoMesh QL-7 detects and what the public safety index displays is substantial and documented. Saltmarsh's commercial contracts with industrial operators include confidentiality provisions that exclude plume attribution data from public disclosure, meaning a factory exceedance event may register clearly in the private industrial feed while the public terminal in the affected neighborhood shows 'Acceptable.' Community health advocates have obtained leaked QL-7 data packets on multiple occasions, and the delta between private and public readings has become a significant point of contention in GLMZ's ongoing environmental accountability disputes.
social_impact: The AtmoMesh QL-7 has created a two-tier reality of environmental knowledge in GLMZ: corporations and industrial operators navigate the city with full atmospheric intelligence while residents in high-exposure districts receive sanitized summaries that systematically underreport hazard events. This information asymmetry has direct health consequences — lower-tier residents show elevated rates of respiratory and neurological conditions consistent with chronic low-level exposure to compounds that the public index regularly rates as safe. The network's dual-use architecture — originally co-developed with Arcturus Defense Solutions for biological agent detection — also means Saltmarsh holds the most comprehensive real-time map of atmospheric conditions in the city, a dataset with obvious military and intelligence value.
story_hooks: A community health collective has built a pirate sensor node that taps directly into the QL-7 mesh and mirrors the unfiltered industrial feed to an anonymous public broadcast — Saltmarsh's legal team and someone else are both trying to find the node

The AtmoMesh has detected a novel compound signature in a lower-district zone for six weeks — it matches no known industrial process, the data is flagged confidential, and three Saltmarsh engineers who reviewed the raw feed have since taken unscheduled leave
A QL-7 sensor node in the transit infrastructure has been physically modified — someone has added a secondary sampling module that doesn't match any Saltmarsh hardware catalog
An Arcturus Defense Solutions subsidiary is negotiating to purchase Saltmarsh's full historical AtmoMesh dataset — twelve years of atmospheric chemical mapping of every district in GLMZ
